capabilities: Sync the vault across desktop and mobile via a private GitHub repository
Encrypt file contents and file names with a password-derived AES-256-GCM key
Merge non-overlapping edits and keep both versions of clashing edits
Sign in to GitHub with a one-time code and set up the repository from settings
Pause, resume, and run sync manually via commands
disambiguation: Despite the name, it is not a git version-control plugin for commits and branches; it uses a GitHub repository only as encrypted sync storage.
extras: Marked 'Beta' with a warning to back up the vault before the first sync; the manifest notes it has not been reviewed by Obsidian staff; full detailed guide exists only in Russian (docs/README.ru.md); files over 50 MB are skipped and the plugin warns near 700 MB of repo size; losing the password makes the GitHub data permanently undecryptable.
motivation: The author wanted sync with 'Your storage, no middleman' — no third-party server, no subscription, and no plaintext on anyone else's servers.
problem: Keeping a vault in sync across devices usually means a paid sync service or a third-party server that can read your notes; this syncs through the user's own GitHub repo so the server only ever sees ciphertext.

relations.evidence: Sync your Obsidian vault across desktop and mobile devices through your own private GitHub repository.

summary: Vault sync through your own private GitHub repository, with password-based end-to-end encryption and conflict-safe merging.
